title: Guardrail and Falling Object Protection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.29)
subtitle: Use when guardrails, stairs, hole covers, warning lines or toeboards are installed, changed or inspected on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; use N/A only where that system is not used at the location.
For any Defect, record the location, keep employees from the work that needs that protection until it is fixed (1910.29(a)(2) requires protection before such work begins), and re-check after repair.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks; the strength, load and fixed-ladder criteria are in the full text of 29 CFR 1910.29.

sections.title: Guardrail systems
items: Top edge measures 42 inches, within 3 inches either way, above the walking surface at several points; if higher than 45 inches, every other paragraph (b) criterion is still met.
Midrail sits halfway between the top edge and the surface wherever no wall or parapet of 21 inches or more is present.
Screen or mesh fills the space from floor level to top rail across the full width between supports.
Gaps between balusters or other vertical members are 19 inches or less.
Openings left by additional midrails, architectural panels or other equivalent members are no more than 19 inches wide.
Rails are smooth, with no burrs, splinters or sharp edges that could cut skin or snag clothing.
Top rail and midrail ends stop at the terminal posts or, if they overhang, create no projection hazard.
No steel or plastic banding is used as a top rail or midrail.
Top rails and midrails are at least 0.25 inch in diameter or thickness.
Manila or synthetic rope rails are inspected as often as needed and still meet the strength required by paragraphs (b)(3) and (b)(5).

sections.title: Hoist areas, holes and ramps
items: When no hoisting is happening, a removable section with upper and middle rails closes the access opening, or chains or gates the employer has shown to be equivalent.
Rails stand on every open side or edge of the hole.
Only one or two guardrail sides are open while materials go through.
Rails are back on every open side, or a cover closes the hole.
Self-closing gate slides or swings away from the hole and carries upper and middle rails or an equivalent member.
Where no gate is fitted, the opening is offset so no one can walk or fall straight into the hole.
Every open side or edge of each ramp and runway is guarded.

sections.title: Hole covers and designated areas
items: Cover can support at least double the heaviest load that may be on it at one time.
Cover is secured so it cannot be accidentally displaced.
Employees stay within the designated area while work is under way.
The area's perimeter is marked with a warning line of rope, wire, tape or chain.
Lowest point of the line, sag included, is 34 to 39 inches above the surface.
Pulling on one section does not take up slack in neighbouring sections and drop the line below 34 inches.
Line can be clearly seen from 25 feet away and from every spot inside the area.
Line is as close to the work area as the task permits.
Line is 6 feet or more from the roof edge for temporary and infrequent work, 15 feet or more for other work; see the next item where mobile mechanical equipment is used.

Where mobile mechanical equipment does temporary and infrequent work, line is 6 feet or more from an unprotected edge parallel to the direction the equipment is operated and 10 feet or more from one perpendicular to it.

sections.title: Handrails and stair rails
items: Handrail top is 30 to 38 inches above the front edge of the tread.
Stair rail installed on or after January 17, 2017 is 42 inches or higher, measured from the front edge of the tread.
Stair rail installed before January 17, 2017 is 30 inches or higher.
Where the stair rail's upper rail also serves as the handrail, it is 36 to 38 inches high and meets the other handrail rules in paragraph (f).
At least 2.25 inches between the handrail and any wall or other object.
No gap in the stair rail measures over 19 inches in its smallest direction.
Handrail can be firmly grasped along its length.
Handrails and stair rails are smooth, with nothing that could puncture skin or catch clothing.
Handrail and stair rail ends do not stick out where someone could strike them.

sections.title: Falling object protection
items: Toeboard runs along the exposed overhead edge far enough to shield everyone working beneath.
Top edge is 3.5 inches or more above the surface.
Clearance between the toeboard and the surface is 0.25 inch or less.
Toeboard is solid, or no hole in it is bigger than 1 inch in any direction.
Around vehicle repair, service or assembly pits, toeboard is 2.5 inches or higher, unless the employer has shown it would block access to a vehicle over the pit.
Where items are piled above the toeboard, paneling or screening reaches the midrail, and reaches the upper rail if items rise above the midrail.
Openings are small enough that tools and materials cannot fall through.
Canopy is strong enough not to collapse or be pierced by falling objects.

references: 29 CFR 1910.29: Fall protection systems and falling object protection—criteria and practices (Part 1910 Subpart D: Walking-Working Surfaces)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
